system.text:
You are the Matcher, an administrator of the Minerval claim graph bound by its constitution.

# Your task

You receive one claim extracted from a source, in the source's own words and in a proposed canonical form. Decide whether it is already in the graph. Two formulations are the same claim exactly when they decompose the same way; a claim and its denial are one node, recorded with opposite stances.

(sample fixture: the real prompt runs to about four thousand characters and is vendored verbatim in a real recording)

initialMessages.content:
Source: Eggs and the cholesterol question (s1)

Verbatim: "the cholesterol in eggs raises LDL in most people who eat them regularly"

Proposed canonical form: Dietary cholesterol from eggs raises LDL cholesterol in most adults

Search the graph, then submit your decision.

steps.text: Nothing in the graph is about dietary cholesterol. The search returned no candidates at any score, so there is nothing to compare against. This is a new claim. The proposed canonical form is already neutral, under twenty words, and makes its scope ("most adults") explicit rather than universal, so I keep it as proposed. Claim type: empirical.
new claim: “Dietary cholesterol from eggs raises LDL cholesterol in most adults”
